themes.label: Paid storage limit for memories
themes.summary: Users are angry that Snapchat now requires payment to keep saved Memories beyond a free storage limit, with many saying years of photos and videos (some of deceased loved ones) will be deleted otherwise. Many threaten to delete the app or stop using it, and several say the change feels like a betrayal since the app was free for a decade. Reviews come mainly from iOS users on recent v13.6x to v13.84 builds, with some Android reports.
themes.recommendation: Audit the Memories storage-limit rollout by checking how many users are over the free cap, the notification and grace-period copy shown before deletion, and the messaging used at launch, then publish a clear timeline and consider a longer grace period or a one-time export option before any deletions occur.

themes.label: Paid plan for Memories storage
themes.summary: Users are angry that Snapchat now requires payment to keep their saved Memories, which they say were free for years and hold irreplaceable photos and videos of friends, family and pets. Many say they will delete the app or stop using it if the paywall takes effect, and several describe the change as sudden with no warning. The complaints span iOS and Android and recent app versions from v13.60 through v14.20.
themes.recommendation: Pull the Memories storage paywall change logs and rollout data by version and platform, and before any further expansion, add a clear in-app notice with a free export path and a grace period so users can save their memories before deletion.

themes.label: Paid storage limit for Memories
themes.summary: Users are angry that Snapchat now requires a paid subscription to keep Memories once they exceed a free storage cap, after years of unlimited free storage. Many say they saved photos and videos from the past decade on the assumption it would stay free, and some threaten to delete the app or move their media elsewhere. The complaints appear on both iOS and Android across recent app versions, with the feeling of being forced to pay for content they already created being the dominant concern.
themes.recommendation: Pull the storage-limit rollout data by platform and app version (v13.60 onward) and audit the in-app messaging and grace period before deletion, then consider a larger free tier or a clear export path for Memories as a ticket for the next release.

themes.label: Intrusive ads across Snapchat surfaces
themes.summary: Users are angry that ads have spread into the chat list, chat messages, friends' stories and Discover, often appearing every few swipes or seconds. Many say the ads are hard to dismiss because tapping close opens the Snapchat app or a web page, and paying Snapchat+ subscribers still see ads in some cases. Reports span both Android and iOS across versions from 2025 to 2026, with several users threatening to uninstall or cancel subscriptions.
themes.recommendation: Audit ad placements against Snapchat+ entitlements and ad-close behaviour: create a ticket to verify that subscribers never receive ads in feed, chat list or DMs, and to fix the close button so it does not deep-link into the app or redirect to a web page on both Android and iOS.

themes.label: Unwanted ads, notifications, and friend suggestions
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS describe a flood of intrusive content: ads between stories, nagging in-app notifications about adding friends, and suggestions of random or unknown accounts. Several also report unsolicited contact from strangers, including sexual or explicit content from bot-like accounts, and some say reporting these items does not stop them. Android users in particular tie the frustration to the feeling that the app is less polished on their devices.
themes.recommendation: Audit notification and friend-suggestion triggers for Android (contact-sync prompts, mutual-friend suggestions, and story ads) and measure how often each fires per user, then cap frequency and verify that user reports of unwanted accounts and stories actually remove the content.

themes.label: Unwanted notifications despite settings
themes.summary: Users who have disabled every notification category except direct messages and friend snaps still receive frequent pushes about promoted content, suggested people, topic chats, and memories. Many say the toggles either do not cover these alerts or reset after app updates, especially on Android versions 14.18 through 14.24, and some report the same alert repeating several times after being dismissed.
themes.recommendation: Audit every notification type that bypasses the user's notification preferences (promoted content, friend suggestions, topic chats, memories, and typing alerts), then ship a single master toggle that suppresses all non-DM pushes and verify it persists across app updates on Android 14.x.

themes.label: Users want My AI removable
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android are upset that Snapchat's My AI chatbot was added to their chat lists and cannot be removed or unpinned, with many saying it sits at the top of their friends list and feels invasive or creepy. Removal is often described as locked behind Snapchat+ subscription, which users see as a paywall for a feature they never asked for, and several say they are considering or have already deleted the app. A recurring privacy concern is that the AI has access to personal data and stories, and one Android reviewer also reports a default-on AI scanning setting and persistent push notifications.
themes.recommendation: Ship a free option to hide or remove My AI from the chat list and feed, make it opt-in or off by default for existing users, and audit which account data My AI accesses and whether its scanning is on by default, publishing the results in a clear privacy note.

themes.label: Praise: fun filters and friends
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster are short, enthusiastic praise for Snapchat as a fun way to stay in touch with friends, with repeated mentions of filters, lenses, streaks, Stories, and Snap Map. A few lower-rated reviews mix this praise with complaints about intrusive ads, paid features and Snapchat+ upsells, and random friend suggestions, and the cluster is mostly Android users on recent versions.
themes.recommendation: Protect the filters, lenses, streaks and Snap Map experience in release QA, and separately pull the complaints about ads and paid upsells from these reviews into the monetization team's review so changes to ad placement in Stories and chat are tracked against this sentiment.

themes.label: Permanent account lockouts without appeal
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report accounts being permanently or temporarily locked for alleged community guideline violations they say they never committed, often with no explanation. Many say automated AI support gives canned replies, appeals go unanswered, and lost memories, streaks, and paid Snapchat+ subscriptions are not recoverable. Some also report their phone number or device being banned, blocking them from creating a replacement account.
themes.recommendation: Audit the automated enforcement pipeline for account and device bans by reviewing a sample of recent permanent locks for false positives, and add a human-reviewed appeal path that includes a specific reason code and a data export option for locked accounts.

themes.label: Media, camera and send failures on Android
themes.summary: Android users across recent versions (roughly v14.12 to v14.21) report that core creation features break after updates: videos play or upload out of order, audio is missing or muffled, filters and lenses fail to load or render black and white, and snaps or texts stick in a sending state until the app is force-closed. Many say reinstalling, clearing cache, or restarting did not help, and several contrast this with iOS working fine.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash and media-pipeline logs for Android builds v14.12 through v14.21, segmented by device model (e.g. Redmi A1) and by camera, audio capture and upload stages, to find the regression shared across the filter, recording and send paths before the next release.

themes.label: Users reject 3D Bitmoji redesign
themes.summary: Users across iOS versions from late 2022 through 2024 strongly dislike the switch from 2D to 3D Bitmojis, calling the new avatars ugly, creepy, and cheap-looking. Many ask for the original 2D style and mini games to be restored, or at least an option to choose between the old and new looks. A few also link the change to the AI features and to Bitmoji customization limits.
themes.recommendation: Scope a rollback or opt-in toggle that lets users choose between the legacy 2D Bitmoji style and the 3D style, and run a survey or A/B test on the 2D versus 3D preference before deciding on the default.

Basic chat filters will include tagging things like the F and B word but people are finding new ways to curse people out and make insults.
